strategies.name: Sequential All-Reduce with Inline Scaling
strategies.desc: Eight consecutive all-reduce calls with local scale/unscale operations fused between them using element-wise ops. Approximately 8 collective dispatches plus local compute kernels. Minimizes code complexity but suffers from sequential latency accumulation across stages with no overlap opportunity.

strategies.name: Vectorized Scale Array Broadcasting
strategies.desc: Precompute all scale coefficients as tensors and use broadcasting to apply per-shard scales in single kernel launches instead of loops over world_size. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but reduces local compute overhead by ~W factor through vectorized operations, trading memory for compute efficiency at large world sizes.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Pipeline
strategies.desc: Decompose each all-reduce into reduce-scatter followed by all-gather, allowing pipeline overlap between stages where gather of stage i overlaps with scatter of stage i+1. Doubles collective count to ~16 dispatches but can hide latency through asynchronous launch and smaller per-op payloads (factor of W reduction in scatter phase).

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction
strategies.desc: Exploit multi-node topology by splitting all-reduce into intra-node and inter-node phases, performing local scaling only after node-local reductions complete. Approximately 16 dispatches (2 levels × 8 stages) but leverages faster intra-node bandwidth and reduces cross-node traffic volume through early aggregation.

strategies.name: Fused Scale-Reduce with Custom Operator
strategies.desc:
Bundle the scale application and reduction into a single collective operation by passing scale factors as metadata to a custom REDUCE_SUM operator that applies per-rank weighting during the reduction tree. Reduces to 8 dispatches with integrated scaling, eliminating intermediate buffers and separate scale kernel launches entirely.
